metadata.question: Is the size of ozone hole (<220 Dobson units) over Antarctica between September 26 and 30, 2024 larger than that between August 26 and 30, 2024?

data.raw_code: The user is asking: "Is the size of ozone hole (<220 Dobson units) over Antarctica between September 26 and 30, 2024 larger than that between August 26 and 30, 2024?" This is about comparing ozone hole area between two time periods. We need to: 1. Search strategy: Use ozone satellite data. NASA provides ozone data through the "OMI/Aura Ozone (O3) Total Column 1-Orbit L2 Swath 13x24km" collection (ID: OMI/Aura/O3_TCL_1r) which has the 'O3' band in Dobson units. We'll need to filter for Antarctica region and the two date ranges. 2. Masking strategy: The ozone hole is defined as area with O3 < 220 Dobson units, so we need to create masks for values < 220 and compute area. 3. Logic: We'll compute the area of pixels with O3 < 220 for each period, then compare. Need to handle cases with no data, no valid pixels, or calculation failures. Challenges: - OMI data might have gaps or be unavailable for specific dates. We should check collection sizes. - We need to compute area accurately over Antarctica using appropriate projection. - The ozone hole is typically measured in September vs August, so we expect data to exist but need to verify. Approach: 1. Define geometry for Antarctica (use a bounding box or polygon covering the region). 2. For each period (Aug 26-30, 2024 and Sep 26-30, 2024): a. Get OMI image collection filtered by date and bounds. b. Check if collection is empty -> try recovery (maybe use different collection? But OMI is the standard for ozone). c. Compute mean ozone for the period (or process each image? For area calculation, we might want to compute daily areas and average, or use the mean image). d. Create mask where O3 < 220. e. Compute area of mask (in km²) using pixel area calculation. 3. Compare the two areas. 4. Output answer with proper tag. Validation: - Check if collections have images. - Check if after masking, there are valid pixels. - Check if area calculations are valid numbers. Fallback: If OMI collection has no data, we might try TOMS data, but OMI should be available for 2024. Let me structure the code accordingly. ```javascript const ee = require('@google/earthengine'); const privateKey = require('../auth_keys/test-project-473922-29f05d49bed7'); async function runAnalysis() { // 1. Geometry & Time Definitions // Define Antarctica region (bounding box covering Antarctica) var antarctica = ee.Geometry.Rectangle([-180, -90, 180, -60], null, false); // Date ranges var augStart = '2024-08-26'; var augEnd = '2024-08-31'; // Exclusive, so up to Aug 30 var sepStart = '2024-09-26'; var sepEnd = '2024-10-01'; // Exclusive, so up to Sep 30 // Function to compute ozone hole area for a given date range function getOzoneHoleArea(startDate, endDate) { // Load OMI ozone data var collection = ee.ImageCollection('OMI/Aura/O3_TCL_1r') .filterDate(startDate, endDate) .filterBounds(antarctica) .select('O3'); var count = collection.size(); var countInfo = count.getInfo(); console.log(`${startDate} to ${endDate} Images: ${countInfo}`); if (countInfo === 0) { // No data for this period return null; } // Compute mean ozone over the period var meanO3 = collection.mean(); // Create mask for ozone hole (O3 < 220 Dobson units) var ozoneHoleMask = meanO3.lt(220); // Calculate area of ozone hole in km² // First, get pixel area in km² (pixelArea gives m², divide by 1e6 for km²) var area = ozoneHoleMask.multiply(ee.Image.pixelArea().divide(1000000)) .reduceRegion({ reducer: ee.Reducer.sum(), geometry: antarctica, scale: 10000, // Use 10km scale for ozone data maxPixels: 1e9 }).get('O3'); var areaValue = area.getInfo(); // Count valid pixels in mask to check for C2 var pixelCount = ozoneHoleMask.reduceRegion({ reducer: ee.Reducer.count(), geometry: antarctica, scale: 10000, maxPixels: 1e9 }).get('O3').getInfo(); console.log(`Valid pixels: ${pixelCount}, Area: ${areaValue} km²`); return { area: areaValue, pixelCount: pixelCount, collectionSize: countInfo }; } // 2. Data Acquisition & Check var augResult = getOzoneHoleArea(augStart, augEnd); var sepResult = getOzoneHoleArea(sepStart, sepEnd); // Check for C1: Empty Collection if (augResult === null || sepResult === null) { console.log(`August data available: ${augResult !== null}, September data available: ${sepResult !== null}`); console.log("C1"); return; } // Check for C2: No Valid Pixels if (augResult.pixelCount === 0 || sepResult.pixelCount === 0) { console.log(`August valid pixels: ${augResult.pixelCount}, September valid pixels: ${sepResult.pixelCount}`); console.log("C2"); return; } // 3. Validation & Final Answer var augArea = augResult.area; var sepArea = sepResult.area; console.log(`August ozone hole area: ${augArea} km²`); console.log(`September ozone hole area: ${sepArea} km²`); // Check for C3: Calculation Failure if (augArea === null || sepArea === null || isNaN(augArea) || isNaN(sepArea) || augArea < 0 || sepArea < 0) { console.log("Invalid area calculation"); console.log("C3"); return; } // Compare areas if (sepArea > augArea) { console.log("A"); } else { console.log("B"); } } async function initEE() { await new Promise((resolve, reject) => { ee.data.authenticateViaPrivateKey(privateKey, resolve, reject); }); await new Promise((resolve, reject) => { ee.initialize(null, null, resolve, reject); }); await runAnalysis(); } initEE(); ```
